title: Courtyard Fountain Plaza Designer
description: The user designs a small architectural courtyard plaza by placing duck fountain sculptures and decorative lanterns along a tiled ground plane. Users click to place lanterns at desired positions, drag duck fountains to anchor points around a central water feature, toggle lantern illumination on/off, and rotate the entire scene to review their composition from different angles.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive courtyard plaza designer. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader: 'shared_assets/Duck.glb' as a fountain sculpture and 'shared_assets/Lantern.glb' as a decorative architectural lantern. Scene setup: Create a 20x20 unit ground plane textured with a procedural checkerboard tile pattern in warm sandstone colors to represent a courtyard floor. Add a simple circular geometry in the center (flattened torus or cylinder) colored blue-gray to represent a shallow fountain basin. Place one initial Duck model scaled appropriately at the center of the basin. Use a soft ambient light (intensity 0.4) and one directional light simulating late-afternoon sun casting across the courtyard. Camera: Use PerspectiveCamera at a 45-degree elevated angle, with OrbitControls for rotation and zoom, min/max distance clamped between 10-40 units. Interactions (4-6 steps): Step 1 - Click a 'Place Lantern' button in an HTML overlay panel, then click anywhere on the ground plane to spawn a Lantern clone at that position (racast against ground). Step 2 - Click a 'Place Duck' button, then click the ground to spawn additional Duck fountain clones (max 4 ducks total). Step 3 - Click any placed lantern to toggle its light: add or remove a warm-yellow PointLight (intensity 2, distance 8) at the lantern's position, and visually indicate active lanterns with a subtle emissive glow on the lantern mesh. Step 4 - Click and drag any placed duck to reposition it on the ground plane using drag controls. Step 5 - A 'Night Mode' toggle button shifts the ambient light to very low (0.05) and directional light off, so only active lanterns illuminate the scene, showcasing the architectural lighting design. Render with tone mapping set to ACESFilmic and outputColorSpace sRGB. Add a subtle shadow from the directional light onto the ground plane using PCFSoftShadowMap. Display a small instruction text overlay explaining the controls.
